utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you again that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you have -- is there any ... given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. File will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we please look at P1900; English page 24, B/C/S page 27. I think we need the next page in the B/C/S, please. So here you see Table 11 which was being discussed on Monday.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You said on Monday at transcript 38212 that the figures for Table 11 on the bottom line, under total, do not add up to 100 per cent; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that they are not 100 per cent accurate. I said the sum was not 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said it was 75 per cent approximately; so, therefore, 75 is not 100. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: But these figures are not supposed to add up to 100 per cent, are they?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can you explain why you believe they should add up to 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I think it; it's a rule. If you have one total mass, and from that total mass, you take out certain shares, then the total mass must amount to 100. If it does not amount to 100, then a footnote must be inserted to explain what's missing in those 100. Because if you look at this and you say 34.2 per cent, of what? Of which mass? You must know the total. And then 19.4 per cent, from which total? All these must add up to 100 per cent. If they do not, you have to explain where the difference lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to what it relates. If you have -- if you say total, it implies that this total contains within itself 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This table shows the proportion of missing and dead Muslim men in five individual municipalities relative to the 1991 census population in each of those municipalities. So imagine a scenario where the proportion in each municipality was 25 percent, if you added up the five figures of 25 percent, you would get 125. The point is that if you add these together you just get a random number. It's not a percentage of anything; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's not right at all. I don't know if I'm explaining this well, but it's an elementary thing called taking out portions out of a mass, which is a total. If, for instance, somebody told you that your income will grow by 34 per cent, you must know 30 per cent of what? And that's going to be your raise. If somebody told you that your salary would be divided according to percentages among four or five persons and how much each of them would receive, that means that 100 per cent must be such and such a number. If somebody says, Each of you will receive 20 per cent, and 20 per cent will go to charity, it still has to amount to 100 per cent of something. If you see a price of an item raised by 30 per cent, you must know the initial price.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I want you to keep in mind the two figures on this page actually and we're going to look at your report. So keep in mind the percentage in the lower right-hand corner of Table 11, which is 14.2 per cent, and also the figure in the lower right-hand corner of the footnote, Footnote 18, which was calculated by removing the unmatched census individuals, which says 12.3 per cent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. File, would you allow me one question. The whole of your answer rests on the assumption that we're talking about one mass. As I read the report of Dr. Tabeau, the first column is about the percentage of the male population of Srebrenica. The second, the 19.4, is 94 per cent of a different mass. That is, the male population of Bratunac. The third, 11.3 per cent, is 11.3 per cent of another mass, which is the male population of Vlasenica. The fourth is 1.9 per cent of the male population of Zvornik. And the fifth is 8.6 per cent of, again, a different mass; that is, the male population of Han Pijesak. Now you have explained clearly to us how, if you have one mass, and if you take portions of that, and if it would cover the whole mass, that you need to get to 100 per cent. That's the pie chart system. You have not explained to us why adding percentages of totally different masses, in your view, also when added, should be 100 per cent. You could have added another ten municipalities and then, of course, there's no logic at all, in my understanding, but please correct me when I'm wrong, that by adding them up, you would end up at 100 per cent because it's not one mass but it's five different masses. You have any comment on this short explanation of how I understand the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's five different masses, then it should not be shown this way, as it was shown by Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. In that case, that mass has to be shown for every municipality, and then it should be 100 per cent for Srebrenica, 100 per cent for Bratunac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'll stop you there. Because you're always telling us that they should have done something different. At the same time, they explained clearly what the masses are on which they calculated percentages. You just ignore that, apparently. Then, confronted with the lack of logic, you say but then they should have presented it otherwise. They clearly said what the masses are in this report. That is, the male population of Srebrenica, the male population of Bratunac, the male population of Vlasenica, and, therefore, you are putting question marks that it doesn't add up to 100 per cent, but there's no -- the whole of your criticism is based on, I'm afraid - I'm carefully in saying - in misunderstanding that these five columns are all in the percentages are all about one mass, all about one total, where it's clearly explained in the report that they are not. Do you have any comment on that, apart from telling us that they should have done something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. First of all, it's not clearly explained in the report. If you read it, beginning with the title, it's not clear. Second, there is a manipulation here. In the table here it says: Population in 1995. I maintain that nobody could calculate the population in 1995. That's one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- if it's not the population of 1995 but in 1990 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you there. You're shifting to a different subject. My question was about the logic of adding up the percentages of what seemed to be different masses. Now whether you think that the definition of the masses is not perfect, that's another matter. But where's the logic of adding those percentages of different masses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Percentage from different masses should not be added up. But, please, if you allow me. There is something in statistic that is called statistical technique. Rules exist as to how to make tables -- all right. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I stop you there. You clearly say percentages from different masses should not be added up and that's exactly the basis for your criticism was. You said, I add them up and it's 75.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the basis for my critique is much broader than just this. But if that's the way you understand it, there's absolutely nothing I can do about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know have you more critical notes, but I was focussing on the one which you specifically expressed and for which you now say that you shouldn't add up those percentages. Mr. File, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As I --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you just allow me one more word --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... wait. Wait. Wait for the next question. If there's anything that should be further explained and is not clear, Mr. Ivetic has an opportunity to re-examine you soon and will put everything straight, if it is not yet. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As I was saying, the percentages I want you to keep in mind are the 14.2 per cent figure in the lower right, the total for Table 11 and then the 12.3 per cent in the footnote for the total -- for Table 11 minus the approximately 1.000 uncensused [sic] matched individuals. We're going to turn to your report, which is D1211 MFI, under seal. And if we could please have English page 58 and B/C/S page 57. So here you have table 9 which says: Proportion of dead/missing men according to the results of the Prosecution, ICMP, ICRC for the area considered to be Srebrenica. Now in the paragraph below that it appears that you've done your own calculation of what the proportion would be if the Prosecution list from 2009 were all dead, and you ended up with 12.8 per cent; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now yesterday you testified about the methodology in this table. That was at transcript page 38276 and the next page. At page 38277, you said: "So to calculate anything in terms of age, et cetera, for Srebrenica and to assess how many inhabitants of Srebrenica there were in Srebrenica, then no one can do that. It can only be done at an aggregate level. This aggregate level is methodologically correct and you can say there was this many in 1991, this many in 1995 went missing, died, et cetera, from the total population of 1991 and this the total number of victims from different areas. It is that percentage, that's it, and this is how it is done." My question for you is if this is how it is done and you get 12.8 per cent, and when Dr. Tabeau performs it according to her own methodology and gets either 14.2 per cent or 12.3 per cent, depending on whether you include the approximately 1.000 people who could not be matched with the census, it seems that your method does not really produce much of a difference in results; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not object to the total or the last column given by Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau. I objected to the age groups, zero to 4, 5 to 9, et cetera. When you are dealing with totals on an aggregate level that's fine. It is a fact that in the total population an age group has a share such and such, et cetera, it's, let's say, 12.8 per cent. But when you say that the population of that age in 1995 in any category was such and such, have you to know the total population in 1995 and then you say out of that total population, the age group 10 to 14 is so much, 45 to 50 is such and such a number. But they do not know the total population in 1995, and nobody knows it. I don't even know anyone who tried to make an estimate. And if you don't know that, it's not possible to determine age groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I also want to ask you about your actual calculation here. This is another place where you rounded down to a lower decimal when you should have rounded up; right? And the basis for that is if you divide 7632 divided by 59674, you get 12.89 per cent. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember now. If you calculated it, it's possible, but that really has nothing do with my desire to decrease something because of some point 000-something per cent. If the second decimal is higher than 5, it's rounded off to a higher digit. This cannot in any case affect the general picture, whether it's 12.5 or 12.8 doesn't change anything. In any estimates made by your experts, I never checked whether they rounded things off to 12.4 or 12.5, and I didn't look at it through that prism, through somebody's desire to diminish something or minimise it. Maybe 1 per cent is important but 100th part of something can hardly change anything. When I work, I always try to round off --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- numbers upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: One other question about this table. It seems that one claim that you have is that the Tabeau report should have broken down the percentages according to the missing and the dead and not put them together in the same figure; right? That's another one of your critiques?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would be more fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they put together the missing and the dead together here, whereas, they could separate them as the ICRC does. That would be more fair because there is no certainty, there is no confirmation that they are dead, although they show them as such in their reports, saying that they have not found any of these persons in voters' registers. That way of showing things is absolute.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So when you broke out those figures in this table under "dead, ICMP," you put 5.061 which comes from the 2009 report. You didn't put 6.603 which is the figure in the 2013 update, P2794. What was your thinking when you decided to do that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean anything bad. I used the report of Dr. Helge Brunborg that I had access to in 2009, and I simply didn't take into account the report from 2013. I just cited the exact source here. If Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau show it that way, I thought that's the way it was. And, still, I don't believe that even if I had cited the 2013 report, it wouldn't have changed the picture much. This is proof of how things should be properly done, and I take over the reports of your experts. I don't think that I -- even if I had changed some number a little, it wouldn't have changed the general picture, and I certainly didn't have any intention to minimise anything. In Dr. Brunborg's report, all these other numbers are also present. Dr. Brunborg cites the ICMP and cites the ICRC as well. His report contains all this data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to the witness, please. You said: "I take over the reports of your experts." This is plural. But you didn't take over the report of 2013. Do you agree on that? You ignored that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I reviewed it. In it, the numbers just explained that the one that they got as identified for the ICMP but both Dr. Brunborg and Dr. Tabeau wrote this report as well, from which I took this data. And now have you to take into account the following. I display everything that they found, the missing, the dead, et cetera, there's no wish to diminish the number. Within this number of the dead and the missing, they are just speaking of the increase in the number of dead persons and I'm not challenging that. I'm showing how it is according to their report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that all the missing are dead --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, going far beyond the scope of my question. I'm just stating that you -- you even said I reviewed the 2013 report but then you didn't take that into account. You ignored the figures. Do you mean the meaning of an update?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. But I did not ignore the figures. Please do pay attention to the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you said: I reviewed it but I used the figures of the 2009 report. That means ignoring. Mr. File, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, I believe [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not all at the same time. Mr Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, I believe the witness is entitled to answer. She started answering at temporary transcript page 12 line 3 before Judge Fluegge interrupted her and then gave the floor back to Mr. File. If there's a question to be asked and the witness is in the middle of answering [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Ivetic. If there's any matter which is not sufficiently clarified have you an opportunity in re-examination to do that. But this witness has shown, time and time again, that she doesn't stay within the scope of the question. Under those circumstances, parties and certainly the Judges, have a possibility and have the discretion of interrupting. And I leave it to that. Mr. File may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, she was interrupted on line number 2 of her answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, this is my ruling. I don't need comments on my ruling. I said Mr. File can put his next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You said that you didn't --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me, if I may. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Ms. Radovanovic, you're here to answer questions. Listen carefully to the next question by Mr. File. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm just going to give you what the figures would be, using your method, if you had used the numbers from 2013 which you said wouldn't have really made much of a difference. If you do your figures, you have it here dividing 5.061 over the total male population of 59.674. As you have in your table you say that's 8.5 per cent. And if you divide 6.603, divided by 59.674, you get over 11 per cent. Do you not consider that a significant difference?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For a simple reason. We are not understanding each other here obviously. The first item in Table 9 says findings of the Prosecution, total and it says 7.692. And all of these findings, although they pertain to the dead and the missing, I show that through 12.8. So I accepted that independently of the increase in the number of dead, as if they were all dead. I did not want to decrease anything. If you see 12.8, that's my finding, that pertains to the total number of the missing and dead, more than shown by the experts of the OTP. So my objective was not to decrease anything but to accept it as if all of that had been proven, that all of these people had been proven dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we please go back to P1900. This time we're going to look at English page 81, B/C/S page 86. Just one question about this table which describes the matching process between the ICRC PHR list and the 1991 census. You mentioned that you thought the first matching criteria were absurd because it would be impossible to match OOD, what you called place of death, with the census of living people. If that were the criteria, you would expect the number of matches here to be zero not 3.325; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this criterion, if the place of death were to be provided and if it requires to have matching with all elements of the key, that is to say to have the name, surname, father's name, and what else was it here? The place of birth, the place of death, if all of that were to be matched, all elements, with the census, then there would be no matches because in the census this element is absent. It is simply not there. That's what I said: The place of death, that is not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So would these results make more sense to you if OOD in this matching key represented an identical match between the municipality of disappearance in the merged ICRC PHR list and the municipality of residence in the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your experts don't say that. They don't say it anywhere. So I don't know what they think.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We don't need this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: On Monday at transcript page 38170 you said that Dr. Brunborg should have collected the raw data from the ICRC in the form of the filled-out missing persons' questionnaires in order to gather more specific information, including about military status and such things. You said he "overlooked it," and you called it "unprofessional." That was at page 38172. Now you might recall that you made the same point back on the 31st of July 2008 when you testified in the Popovic case. If we could look at 65 ter number 33031, please, which as you will see is the transcript of your testimony from that day. If we could go to e-court page 33. Starting at line nine, my colleague, Ms. Soljan, put to you the testimony of Dr. Brunborg in that case who was asked whether he had the raw information from the questionnaires. He is quoted --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to read it to you. Dr. Brunborg is quoted, starting at line 24 as saying: "Yes, I think I have the questionnaire, an empty blank questionnaire, but as I told you just now we did not get that other information. ICRC is very" -- Goes on to say: "... protective about the information they are releasing, to preserve the neutrality so they have access to all sides in a conflict." Then when asked whether he requested it, he answered: "We made general requests for information and I believe it was denied but we could only get the information that had already been provided in electronic format. For example, there was also on the questionnaire, they asked about ethnicity, which was not provided to us. Then you, Ms. Radovanovic, were asked: "So you did not hear this testimony, madam?" And your response was: "Yes, I heard it, and precisely on the basis of this question, I based my conclusion that Dr. Brunborg may have asked for this material, but that he did not see a single questionnaire that had been filled in, and that Dr. Brunborg was happy with the electronic format that was given to him, And that perhaps he did not persist enough in his efforts to get it." So, Dr. Radovanovic, you actually already know the reason why they couldn't get the ICRC questionnaires, because you heard it directly from Dr. Brunborg in his testimony in that case. Did you forget about that on Monday when you said that he overlooked it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object. He needs to read the whole answer if he's going to ask about prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to read the remainder of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: "But on the basis of what Dr. Brunborg said, that the justification that the ICRC decided to treat this material as confidential, is not logical enough. "If the Red Cross places on the Internet the first name, second name, date of birth, place of birth, father's name, and all the other -- or various other attributes, why would they conceal ethnicity or professional background? And if they thought that this material could not be posted on the Internet, even if that were true, I can find it hard to believe that they would refuse to place this material at the disposal of an institution such as the ICTY." So my question for you is: You were aware of the reason why they couldn't get the ICRC questionnaires. Did you forget about that on Monday when you said that he "overlooked it"?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not forget that. You read it yourself what Dr. Brunborg says. We -- he doesn't know what the answer is, so, in the meantime, he could have seen whether they had been refused or not. I continue to believe that the reasons mentioned by Dr. Brunborg are not logical. I believe that this Tribunal has such authority that it managed to obtain materials that are never given to anyone in the world. For example, censuses according to individual data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're again moving away from the question. The question simply focussed on whether you said he overlooked it, whether you had at that moment had on your mind that he explained why, and apparently Mr. File considers overlooking something different than for reasons stated, right or wrong, not to have obtained the materials. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going ask you about one other subject that you have discussed in your testimony and in your report, which is the notion that you claim that the Prosecution experts show a broader context and longer duration for all of the phenomena, and specifically in your report at page 20, in both versions, you say the fact that there are no data sources for the requested specific time when certain demographic phenomena were already occurring is not decisive for them. So we're talking about the forcible displacement report, and I would ask you that you are aware that there are some aggregate numbers from counts that RS authorities did during the conflict; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what have you in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we have 1D02454, please. 1D02454.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As this comes up, you will see that are the minutes of the 70th session of the RS government dated 19 May 1993 covering the previous day's session chaired by Prime Minister Lukic? If we could go to English page 7 and B/C/S page 5, please. Under item 12 in the middle of the page, you see there was a debate on the population census in Republika Srpska and the measures that have to be taken in this regard. And then can you see that they list the data that the census will collect, including first and last name, father's name, date of birth, national affiliation. And then at the bottom it goes on to say: "It is concluded that the Republican Bureau of Statistics of Republika Srpska is to be the co-ordinator and organiser of the overall activity of the census" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. "And that the executive committees are to be the co-ordinators and organisers of censuses in the areas of their respective municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Are you aware that that effort was undertaken in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that whether I agree that a census was carried out in 1993? I don't know exactly what you mean by the verb that you used.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm just asking whether you know about this 1993 census --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for discussions of a census and the possibility that it would be carried out, I heard of that. But I'm not aware of it actually being carried out and that this information was published regarding a population census in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D02454 receives exhibit number P7519, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I decide on admission, you have read a small portion of this document. Do we need the whole of the document in evidence because then the Chamber would have to -- is there any way to have an extract with cover pages, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That would be possible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then, Mr. Ivetic, if the Defence would have any wishes for contextualisation, then ... then I take it upon having received the selection the Prosecution considers relevant that you would add whatever you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It will be marked for identification, pending the upload of an extract on which the parties can agree. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're already going to be having coffee so we can add it to the agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You haven't had it yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 33013, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So on the first page, you can see this is the RS Republican Bureau of Statistics document send to the RS government dated 17 September 1994 titled: Further information on the population census conducted in 1993. If we can go to English page 2 at the top and in B/C/S it's the second paragraph after heading 1. It says: "The census was prepared and conducted in the territory of Republika Srpska under the uniform methodological guidance of experts from the Republican Bureau of Statistics in Banja Luka." It goes on to describe the first results and clarify the information that was reported. It says: "The first results established the number of households, the number of inhabitants according to religion and citizenship, the number of displaced persons and the number of refugees for each populated place, municipality, and the republic according to the administrative and territorial divisions on the day of the census, which was 15 June 1993. The first results were not published but were given to the government for its internal use together with the report on the census, number 153/93 of 7 August 1993." Now from your experience working in census administration, this is how it normally works; right? There is aggregate data presented first for initial reporting and then more detailed information comes later; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first results are published and always as aggregate data. Until they are officially published, it is not valid. Internally carrying out a census that doesn't mean a thing. But information is always disclosed a month or a month and a half after the census itself, and in aggregate form at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In your census experience, when you received the first figures and then there were checks and the figures eventually published later, how different from the revised figures from the initial figures?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends. In the meantime, there's a check and then if the check shows that -- well, according to certain methods according to which this check is carried out then the first results should not vary significantly from the final results. When I say that they shouldn't differ to a significant degree, the census contains a number of questions and at aggregate level there's, after all, total number of inhabitants. But certain questions can be done poorly so then they are not published. So not each and he have question that is it contained in the population census is done with extreme precision. So when the first results are checked that is stated before publishing the final results and such things did happen. There were questions that did not meet the criteria in terms of representing valid information. However, in general terms, if criteria are satisfied, then, yes, they should not vary considerably. The total number of inhabitants, in terms of the final result as compared to the previous results, however, certain characteristics can be considered to be done poorly and then that is not published. For example, mistakes concerning professions, occupations and --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just to be clear, a question such as what is your ethnicity, that's not among the questions that is likely to be considered a poor question that will produce poor data; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. You have entire studies that discuss the matter. Namely, whether the question regarding ethnicity -- rather, answers are good or bad. That is a pending issue. So you can declare yourself whichever way you want: In one census, this way, and in another census, that way. And you don't have to declare yourself at all. Even in the census of 1991, the questionnaire says: According to such and such an article of the constitution, this question does not have to be answered. The question regarding ethnicity is a subjective one. If I feel a certain way or if I'm afraid to say how I feel, I can, but I don't have to answer that question and I don't have to keep continuity in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter number 32461, please. As this comes up, you will see this is a 3 August 1994 Prijedor public security centre document. In the text at the beginning, it says: "Please be informed that we have conducted a census (registration) of non-Serbian population in the municipality area, for the internal purposes of the Ministry of Interior. The census was conducted thoroughly, by going door to door, and the aim was to establish the overall number of the non-Serbian population in order to be able to make a proper security assessment." Then it goes on to say: "We point out that the data should be taken as 99 per cent accurate and we have in our possession the lists with the data for the individual villages." And then have you the breakdown of the non-Serb population. If we go to page 2. There you have the figures. So there was also this kind of census happening as well, done for security reasons; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably. It says here the Ministry of Interior. But they did not publish this anywhere. These are documents that were used internally. I cannot assess them this way, whether they're good or bad, if I don't know according to which methodology they were carried out. How people were registered and what people said, what they were, or what they were not. In order to say that a census is proper, you have to know what the methodology used was. Now somebody saying that 99 per cent of it is correct, the only thing I can say is that that is what is written there. If I read this properly, there is a police document. That's not called a census from a statistical point of view, that is, or they'd have to say for which purposes and so on. Maybe this is some kind of questionnaire. It's not a population census and it's not that within that I'm asking you to tell me what your ethnicity is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that document, and then I have just one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32461 receives exhibit number P7520, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. File, if is really your last question, we'll hear the answer to that question before the break. Otherwise, we'd have to take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We will need to switch back to the witness's report to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: D1211, please. English and B/C/S page 24, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In the top paragraph, the main paragraph there you say, "The absurdity of declaring the voters' registers to be post-war lists of survivors, regardless of which report is in question, is reflected in the experts 'ideas offered to the Tribunal which lead to the logical conclusion that anyone from the 1997/1998 voters' register and the 1991 population census who is not matched is proven to be dead." My question for you is: In reality, to take the voters' lists as an example, Dr. Tabeau is simply saying that they are evidence of a subset of the people who were most likely alive in 1997 and that it's worth checking just to be safe to see whether anyone on a missing list is also on the voters' list but no one is saying that it is a comprehensive list of probable survivors of the conflict and that not being on that list proves you were dead in 1997. Isn't this a mistake in logic that you're making here?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. In his earlier reports, as in the last one, Dr. Brunborg claims that they compared their list with the voters' registers and replying to some previous remarks made that the voters' registers have been made up, they answered by saying, no, there are no living people still proving that our data is correct. Dr. Tabeau states that voters' registers are never taken into account by official statisticians to make calculations, saying that these -- or such information is not official statistically. If on the one hand you have proof there are no survivors because they were not found on the voters' registers, and I can quote that, I can find it in some of the previous reports as well as in the last one. And if, at the same time, madam doctor says that the voters' registers are not official statistical data, they refer to them for the most part as survivors. The list of survivors. Since -- or how can a voters' registers which only includes a part of the population be called a list of survivors? That is what I based my conclusions on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further. We'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. That's five minutes to 11.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Over the break I realised I did not tender 65 ter number 33013 which is the RS Bureau of Statistics document regarding the 1991 census. I would tender that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objection. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33013 receives exhibit number P7521, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give you an opportunity to cross-examine the witness, Mr. Ivetic, Judge Fluegge would have a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, could you please explain for me the difference between the place where a specific person was last seen alive and the place of disappearance? What is the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, according to Dr. Brunborg's definition. As he defines it in all his report, the place of disappearance is supposed to be place where someone was last seen alive but it doesn't seen that it is also the place of death. I'm paraphrasing but it can be read in the report. It could so happen that the VRS arrived, place a person in a vehicle and take them elsewhere. The place of disappearance, when reported to the Red Cross by the relatives, they did so according to what they could hear, learn of, or were told about somebody's -- somebody last being seen somewhere. In other words, the place of disappearance need not be the place where the death occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. But yesterday you said - this can be found on page 38330, line 24 and 25: "That's the place where the person was last seen alive. It's not place of disappearance." And I just wanted to know what is the difference between place of disappearance. I'm not talking about place of death but of disappearance and the place where the person was seen alive. I take it now from your answer that these two are identical; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they're not. I don't know in what context I referred to the place of disappearance. Perhaps I was explaining a table. I'm simply relaying to you Dr. Brunborg's definition of place of disappearance. It is defined as the place where somebody was last seen alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That is exactly what I was hinting at. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During cross-examination, you were asked about the DEM2T and this was at transcript page 38338 and onwards. Could you please clarify for us again this is what database, the DEM2T?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The DEM2T is a database about mortality between 1992 and 1995. On the orders of the Tribunal it was done by the statistical institute of Republika Srpska and of the Federation. It is the official database created according to all statistical standards, especially when it comes to the database of Republika Srpska, Dr. Brunborg praises it as a sound base. As of 2004, the data contained therein is with the Demographic Unit of the Tribunal, where I saw it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you to clarify. In the transcript we have as of 2014 and I'm not sure actually which you said in the original Serbian. Could you please clarify for us when is the data contained in the DEM2T was within the -- within the --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The data gathered was gathered according to all the relevant standards pertaining to the statistics of those who passed away in the period 1992 to 1995. In other words, it is a database about deceased persons between 1992 and 1995 and all the years in between, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say in 2004, the data contained therein and you state the name of the unit at the Tribunal where this data resides. Could you please clarify that unit that you mentioned at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Demographic Unit of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to look at D1211, MFI, under seal, and we should not broadcast this document. And we'll be looking for page 37 in the English, page 36 and 37 in the Serbian. While we wait, Professor, I think that you'll see that this is this your table number 2. And you were asked about this table and this part of your report from transcript page 38338 onwards. Now, first of all, Professor, I'm going to ask you not to mention any of the names on this table in open court. Is that first part understood?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in cross-examination, it was said that a cursory review of the databases by you led to these 31 names. Could you tell us when it was that you performed the cursory review of the databases to find these names.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in The Hague in 2006 or 2007 to check the material. That is when I had occasion to see it. It was in The Hague in the Demographic Unit of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now when you say you did a cursory review of the databases, what databases are you talking about that yielded these results?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the DEM2T database as well as the database on the soldiers of the ABiH and the list of the Prosecution containing the names of the people they considered to be Srebrenica victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at your table which we have before us, we see that we have a column that you have labelled as "went missing on Prosecution," and all those dates are in 1995 from, it looks -- from July through the late part of September 1995. And then on the far right, you have a column that says "date of death," and it lists for these same individuals dates which occur before the date of disappearance in the prior column. Can you tell us, first of all, where does the date of death in the far right column come from?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the dates that can be found in the DEM2T and the ABiH databases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Professor, for the column that says "went missing on Prosecution," where does that data come from?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It comes from the list of victims, according to the OTP, the 7.000-plus people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, throughout the cross-examination, Mr. File took issue with you for allegedly not taking into account the 2013 integration report and that was said to be P2794. I'd like to call up but not broadcast P2794. And if we could turn to page 8 in both versions, again, Professor, we should not identify any of these names that we see before us, but looking at this page we see a table listing a total of six persons. For these six persons, I don't see any information updating their date of disappearance as recorded in the DEM2T or the ABiH list. Therefore, Professor, does any of this data that we see now before us at all change your conclusions that the OTP experts have people on their list for whom the ABiH or Ministry of Defence said they disappeared or died in the years prior to July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask that the table be enlarged. I can't read it well. The table is in English, but I think I understand it well enough. There's nothing I would change. Although I cannot compare it to the other table, but on this list, we have one, two, three, four -- six names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now, P2795 was the other annex in relation to this that Mr. File did not use. I place on the record that P2795, which is not in e-court and which I cannot therefore show, does not have a column relating to the Ministry of Defence ABiH lists and only has a column for date of disappearance without citation to source, listing the same dates that you had, professor, in your table, number 12 that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to this as improper argument and furthermore I would add that we can put this on Sanctions if [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution not stipulating that that is correct? Are you refusing to stipulate that I have correctly identified the columns?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. I have no idea about 2795. In e-court, indeed, it gives an error message and therefore I'd like to know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's pull it up in Sanction. I don't know how to do that, Your Honours. Oh, it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar says that we have P2795 in e-court. I had difficulties in opening it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a surrogate sheet. If there's any substance which could be shown, I don't know if it is public or not. I have got no idea. Could we have a look at it so that we understand what we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it should not be broadcast, to err on the side of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could look at the headings and I will read them for you for the columns. The first one says ID. The second one says names, original. The third one says date of birth. Column D says protocol ID. Column E says case ID. Column F says ID ICMP. Column G says site name. Column H says site co-ordinates. Column J says date of submission. Column K says days of disappearance. And, again, does not list of source. Column L says place of disappearance. And, again, does not list the source. M says type of report. N says ICMP comment. O says BAZ-(OTP 2009) integrated (2013). P says integrated new and less certain (2013). And Q says Dups in 2013. So we only have one column that says date of disappearance that does not give a source and I believe the dates of disappearance are the same as we just saw that you reported in your report based upon the Prosecution's list. If I am wrong, I invite Prosecution counsel to correct me. But working -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I just refer the Tribunal to P1901 which is the OTP list which contains that information at page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1901. If that is the answer then we would also like to have a look at P1901.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not the answer to my question, but, it's, I believe, where this table is said to have even come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get -- do I understand that the issue now is for six out of the 30 persons where the information about the date of death would be prior to July 1995, that for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I missed it. And I would not even mind if you briefly explain what exactly we're discussing at this moment in such a way that it's not inappropriate to do before a witness or otherwise clarify the issue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution during cross-examination made repeated reference to the 2013 list which we've now seen comprises two parts. The first part of the six names which has no data on date of disappearance so it has no affect as to what we just looked at from the witness's report. That's the Defence position. The second annex that we just looked at contains only one date of disappearance which is from the Prosecution list which is already reflected in the table that Professor Radovanovic did and has no data on the military lists which was the point of the report and the table presented by Professor Radovanovic. That is where we are at now and can then I go to some specific issues with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For proper understanding, Mr. File, do you think that we shouldn't look at P1901 or can we do -- or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'll let Mr. Ivetic do his examination as he wants to. If something has to be cleared up I can ask questions later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this which we have in front of us, the 2013 report, this is what Dr. Tabeau said about this report and how it was created and this is at transcript page 19241, lines 6 through 12. I will read it: "A. The 2013 Srebrenica report I made focuses exclusively on the analysis of new identifications issued by the ICMP between the time the 2009 integrated report was finished until February 2013. This was the date I used for my report for the Mladic case. So, in total, there was 1.190 new identifications in this period. Of this number, quite a considerable portion have been additionally matched with the 2009 OTP victims' list." Now, Professor, Dr. Tabeau has indicated the exclusive focus of this 2013 report was new identifications by ICMP. Would DNA identifications by ICMP change your opinions which are based upon data in the DEM2T and the army records of the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina as you have set forth in your report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These people were identified and I never disputed that they were dead. I only disputed the date of death, according to the reports of the army and DEM2T database, as well as -- as per the date as specified on the OTP list as the date of someone's disappearance. One cannot die before disappearing or disappear after death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness also answer the question: What is the approximate percentage or number where such inconsistencies are still remaining?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no occasion after 2007 or 2008 to go and see it. And even if I did, given the time I'm usually given, which is between three and five days, I cannot go into utmost detail. I can only stop at points where I come across a certain figure that I consider sold evidence. In order do things in detail, one requires time. And then, after that, I would be able to tell you on this or that list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Upon your cursory review, that is approximately 30 cases mentioned in your report. Is there any reason to believe that the size of these errors, that the number or percentage would be -- would be different or considerably different from what you found and wrote down in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally have reason to believe that the number, actually the percentage, is considerably higher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's the basis for that belief? And rather -- you say "belief." I would rather have reasons, logical reasons than what is to be believed to be the case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I carry out comparisons and when I come across certain example, I no longer engage in detailed comparisons nor I do introduce new criteria. I provide the most accurate criterion requiring the name, the name of father, last name, the precise date of birth, and so on and so forth. If I expanded my criteria, I would probably come across a larger number of cases and then, like the OTP experts, I could rely on my visual selection to determine whether it is possible or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that goes beyond the date of disappearance compared to the date of the death.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not follow you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're explaining that you believe or think that by names, et cetera, to include all that and to be very precise, that may increase the numbers. But my question was solely focussed on what seems to be a discrepancy between the date of -- between July 1995 and the date of disappearance or the date of death. Rather, the date of death, I would say. That's a rather limited approach, and I think that was the core of the table you presented. And my question now is: In your explanation, did you go beyond what was the focus of my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's possible that we don't understand each other well. When comparison is made, I have the Prosecution list and I set the criterion which says name, father's name, date of birth. That criterion applies to DEM2T and the BH army lists, and I inserted and let all these persons coincide. When they do coincide, then they bring all the other data with them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see Svetlana Radovanovic born on such and such a date and when I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stop you there. Perhaps I should put my question more clearly. We have seen in your report on page 37 in the English the table which presents approximately 30 cases of a reported death which was prior to July 1995. That's the core of the issue in that table. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. DEM2T does not record alleged deaths. It's a database of statistics --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- commissioned by this institution, according to all the professional standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I never used the term "alleged death." I was just referring to the table where I say that the core of the table apparently is that there's a discrepancy because the persons, having been found in the BiH army list and DEM2T to have died before July 1995 are, if I understand you well, incorrectly categorised as Srebrenica victims. That's the core of the table, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, my question -- so it was limited, my question, in its scope, to the date of death compared to categorising the persons as Srebrenica victims, and you gave approximately 30 examples of that, as you said, after a cursory review. Now, since 2009, approximately thousand new identifications have made, if I understand the evidence well. My question was whether there's any reason to believe that such inconsistencies, that is, date of death being reported in the list of the BiH army and DEM2T before July 1995, whether the approximate percentage of death for those last thousand cases would considerably differ from the 30 out of the -- well, I'm just giving a rough figure 6.000 approximately, or 5.000, perhaps, at that time. That is, on the basis of what you established, it's less than 1 per cent. Is there any reason to believe that for the new identifications that that percentage merely on this issue would be higher or lower?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you're asking me to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until I review the material, I can't say anything with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. So you don't know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hate to disappoint you, but the very next area I was going to go into before Your Honour started asking questions is precisely the data which shows that there are even more than 30 in the prior set before the new. So we'll see all the documents. You have already seen them, but I'll remind Your Honours of that and we'll go through that. So your questions will be answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm usually -- whether there are more or less, of course, this Chamber is especially interested in the rate of errors and whether they were properly corrected, yes or no, if new information was there. And that seems to be one of the issues touched upon where this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and we'll -- at the same time the witness said she couldn't tell us for the new ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the old ones and I'm going to show her the documents and I think it will be rather clear for everyone. Because she said can't guess without having looked at the material and we have Dr. Tabeau's material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, before we add - and, of course, I'm looking forward to see that - are we talking about -- and is there any way that the parties could agree that there are another 10 or 20 or 100 or 1.000 mistakes having reviewed the material? Mr. File, Mr. Ivetic. Because the Chamber would be without knowing all the details if the parties agree that there are addition to the 30 here inconsistencies. I'm not yet talking about what explains the inconsistency. It could be a wrong report or a wrong qualification as Srebrenica victims, I have no idea. Or whatever it is. But could the parties seek to agree on what, approximately, the size of the additional mistakes is - --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have that in evidence. It's D411.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- yes. And I hope you'll understand that I have not every single piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I will be presenting it to the witness, so we'll all be reminded of that and we'll go through it step by step and we'll see that what is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We will see that D411 is not a current document and so this is something that we could look into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic. Please move on and we'll further hear the evidence you elicit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now first just to finish up on the issue of ICMP DNA identifications, yesterday you were shown P7513 and I'd like to -- no, first of all, before we go there. Looking at the 2003 [sic] report which we have up on our screens. Whoops, we just lost it. Looking at the 2013 that we have on our screens now, if the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina still has a different registered date of death that occurred before the date of disappearance in this Prosecution list, would that be a continued cause for concern, according to you, as to the reliability of the Prosecution's list?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can look at P7513 and not broadcast the same, and when we get to that document we'll be looking at page 5 in the Serbian, and since page 5 in the Serbian is entirely in English, I propose we only look at that page, and this was presented yesterday at transcript page 38327 as an ICMP data report for this individual. Now, we see that there is nowhere in this report a reference to date of disappearance or date of death, and you said in relation to this report, at transcript page 38326 through 38327 and I quote: "I see this is a DNA report confirming that it was, indeed, that person we discussed earlier and nothing more." Later at transcript page 38333, you said: "I did not see any other evidence because DNA does not prove when and where someone died. DNA proves identity." Now, given the type of data that is contained in ICMP DNA matching reports and given your prior testimony, do you think that looking at additional ICMP DNA matching from 2003 [sic] allows anyone to determine anything about the date of death and date of disappearance?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I object to this question as argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How is it argumentative?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please rephrase the question, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Argumentative with whom. I'm not arguing with anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the ruling is rephrase your question. Do it or move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, if the ICMP DNA report only establishes identity of someone and as we've seen does not have any date of death or date of disappearance, of what assistance can it be in determining date of death or date of disappearance, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not of any assistance for determining the date of death and the date of disappearance or the place of disappearance, because experts, such as Dr. Parsons, say, at this Tribunal, DNA analysis does not help establish the place and time of death. DNA analysis helps determine only identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to look at D344 but not broadcast the same. While we wait for that document, I can introduce it by saying you looked at it a few days ago and you told us at transcript page 38264 as follows about this document: "So, in 2008, the Demographic Unit reacted to a Defence request confirming that there were soldiers on their list and that they matched some 70.1 per cent of overall cases. There were also 228 cases of soldiers for whom the ABiH claimed had been killed before 1995 and yet they were on the list as Srebrenica victims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you please repeat the percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm reading from the transcript, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. And you read the percentage 71 or.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 70.1 -- oh, I apologise. I see now what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you repeat that percentage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's see where I left off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "In this reply, they state that they looked into those 220-plus cases and that, in the meantime, they requested clarifications from the ABiH. They also state that in some 137 cases or so, they received confirmation that the date was incorrect and that it was corrected. They also state that in a certain number of cases, the ABiH did not state whether they were killed or not. In another 38 cases, no reply was received and they were still awaiting one." Now, first of all, do you remember that part of your testimony a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness, he'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, yes, please -- could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. File, I raised a question in private session before the break about the status of certain exhibits. Any answer to that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, the second one, indeed, should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: The list of names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And which is -- which number is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's P2795.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5 is hereby put under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could please take a look at but not broadcast D411, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, again, we should be careful not to mention anyone's name, but if we count up 14 from the bottom of the list, I think we will see the same individual we just looked at in private session who has listed there as the date of death, according to the military records, 15 May 1992, and the column for corrected DOD is blank. That is to say, there is no correction. Now, as to this document, Dr. Tabeau said as follows, that this came after the 2008 inquiry and let me just find the area. It's transcript page 19443 to 19444, and Dr. Tabeau said as to this list: "Where we see a yes in English, y-e-s, under clarification requested in the table, this means that the Prosecution did not receive any new information from the BiH Ministry of Defence as to the date of death." And, in fact, she said that shortly after the request, they were told the ministry was unable to provide any corrections. Bearing in mind if we could look at the individual we just looked at, 14th from the bottom, and for this one, the Prosecution did not even seek any clarification as to the date of death. Given this information, do you have any comment and does this change any of the opinions that you expressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I continue to believe that certain persons are on the Prosecution list, certain persons who had lost their lives before 1995 as the Prosecution states here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to clarify one point in the previous question. It was asked that for this one the Prosecution did not even seek any clarification as to the date of death. I don't believe there's been any evidence that whether the Prosecution sought information is included in that table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Ivetic was referring to the testimony of Dr. Tabeau, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore, the issue is -- not whether there's evidence but whether Dr. Tabeau said so. Because her words are in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we have the table itself which the line says clarification requested and it's either yes or blank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what blank means, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we need to have explained and it was 443 and 444, 19000; isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What was 444?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That particular part at 19444, lines 15 through 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, examined by Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: By me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By you and Ms. Marcus being present for the Prosecution. Let me see. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this list we're looking at now, D411 under seal, on 18 November 2013, Ms. Maxine Marcus of the Prosecution said at transcript page 19444, line 15 through 24, that this was the chart that should replace the one in P1900 which is the 2009 report of Drs. Tabeau and Brunborg. Now looking at the list and just the first page of this list and I can state it has five pages in total, but on the first page of this list I count a total of 50 individuals. Are you following me so far?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For these 50 individuals, some we see new dates of death under the column DOD corrected. But for the remainder, I see -- excuse me, 11 individuals who have dates of death prior to July 1995 where there is no new date of death corrected and there is a yes in the column, meaning clarification was requested and none received by the Prosecution. Are you following me so far?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For 14 more, we see that there is no corrected date of death and we're left with just the date of death prior to July 1995, and we see a yes in the column that -- that clarification was requested, and we see an ICMP protocol and an ICMP grave-site identified for these individuals. Are you following me so far?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And there are an additional five persons with dates of death recorded in the years prior to July 1995 where we don't have any corrected date of death and we don't have anything in the column that says clarification requested, that there is no yes. Are you following me thus far?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, that makes, just on the first page alone, 30 out of 50 individuals where their date of death as recorded by the military occurs prior to July 1995. Does the data as reflected thus far on this chart change any of the concerns and opinions that you expressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly. That is already 50 persons for whom the army did not confirm that they lost their lives in July 1995 but considerably before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To make sure you got my translation correctly there are 30 persons on the first page for whom even after seeking the results that the OTP sought from the Ministry of Defence we still have dates of death before July 1995. I have not gone through any of the other pages, but I can tell you that there are more on those pages as well, but I don't know the numbers. Does that cause you to change your conclusions as to your report, as to the concerns you expressed about the reliability of the Prosecution's lists of victims?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am still concerned about the list of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I had not go through each page to do the arithmetic. I think all of us are free to do that ourselves. But I'd like to look at specific entries, again, without naming the individuals involved. The last time we did this, we used the ICMP protocol numbers which are found on the second-to-last column on the right. And I would like to look at ICMP protocol number 1940/03 and this will be the 20th individual from the top and for this individual we see the date of death for the military as 17, 04, 995. Now that means April 17th, 1995, according to what the Prosecutor told us before the break. That happens to be my birthday but that's irrelevant. We see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll put it on the record, Mr. Ivetic, and we'll take care of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We see that for this individual there is nothing in the column clarification requested and we see that this individual was exhumed from the Liplje 2 grave. And does that information cause you to change any of the findings or opinions that you expressed in your report as to the reliability of the Prosecution's victim lists?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still maintain that the list is unreliable, and this just shows me that persons who lost their lives before July 1995 could have been found in the graves that are linked to Srebrenica. The fact that somebody was found in that grave does not prove that he had lost his life in relation to Srebrenica and up until the end of July, as Dr. Brunborg took it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question in that respect. If you find someone in a grave together with a lot of other persons for which there are good reasons to believe that they died in July 1995 in Srebrenica, if you found one person who's reported as having died well before that date, perhaps even a year before, would you say that doesn't prove he died with the others, I have no difficulties in accepting that, what are the options? I can think of two options to start with, but please add another one. Either he died a year earlier or two years earlier and in one way or another, still unexplained, he ended up in that mass grave where you say that, in itself, doesn't prove anything.
